Please note that members of the public will be allowed to observe and/or address the City Council Meeting of September 22, 2020, at 1:00 P.M. for
closed session as follows:

  1.  Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for consideration by the Inglewood City
  Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending
  them to the City Clerk/Secretary at yhorton@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk aphillips@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure
  distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit comments prior to 8:00 A.M. the
  day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate
  the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received after 8:00 A.M. and prior to the close of the public hearings, will be made part of
  the official public record of the meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310- 412- 5280 with any questions.

  2.  By Telephone - Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members of the public can participate in the meeting by
  telephone to listen and make comments by using the following:

  l Dial - In: 1 - 669- 900- 6833 (Meeting ID: 996 1738 7790; Passcode: 5111).

  l If you are dialing in from a cell phone, please call from an area with good reception. Calls from landline phones are highly recommended.

** The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to address the Legislative Body on Closed Session Items.

  the official public record of the meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310- 412- 5280 with any questions.

  2.  By Telephone - Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members of the public can participate in the meeting by
  telephone to listen and make comments noting the following:

  l The conference begins at 1:30 p.m., Pacific Time, and all interested parties may join the conference 5 minutes prior.
  l If you are dialing in from a cell phone, please call from an area with good reception. Calls from landline phones are highly recommended.
  l If you are watching the meeting via Facebook Live or Channel 35 while also accessing the phone line, it is requested that you mute the

  ¡ September 29, 2020 – Access Code: 2424497# (wait 5 seconds and press # again)

  3.  Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:

  l On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider for details.
  l Live on - line through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video, at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/.

The above access options provide the public with the opportunity to both observe and listen to the meeting; however, members of the public who
wish to orally address the Legislative Body must use the public access options 1 and 2 noted above.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate alternative formats

minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  September 22, 2020

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
September 22, 2020, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:00 p.m.
The Acting City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales
  and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Aisha Thompson  Acting City Clerk
  Artie Fields  City Manager
  Ken Campos  City Attorney

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEM. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on
Closed Session Item No. CS-1.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed Session Item
No. CS-1.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority, at the
hour of 2:00 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.

City/Successor Agency / Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
item on the Agenda.

Gil Mathieu, District 4, spoke concerning the Warrant Register, and Agenda Item No.
DR-2, Agreement with 715 Marlborough Apartments, LLC.
 142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Dotson that
  the demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  September 17, 2020, in the amount of $6,033,047.40, are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AGREEMENT NO. 20-265 APPROVED – HF&H CONSULTANTS, LLC. Staff
  report dated September 22, 2020, was presented recommending approval of a three-year
  agreement with HF&H Consultants, LLC, to provide ongoing solid waste monitoring
  consulting services for the period covering December 1, 2020 to November 30, 2023.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Franklin
  that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 20-265 in an amount not to
  exceed $243,000 ($79,000 for the first year; $81,000 for the second year; and $83,000 for
  the third year). The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

131.8  AGREEMENT NO. 20-266 APPROVED – HOUSING RIGHTS CENTER. Staff
  report dated September 22, 2020, was presented recommending approval of an agreement
  with Housing Rights Center to provide fair housing counseling and housing
  discrimination services for Fiscal Year 2020-2021.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Franklin
  that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 20-266 in the amount of
  $64,500. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101  PRESENTATION OF THE PROPOSED ANNUAL BUDGET FOR FISCAL YEAR
  2020-2021 RECEIVED AND FILED. Staff report dated September 22, 2020, presented
  the proposed annual budget for Fiscal Year 2020-2021.

  Artie Fields, City Manager, provided a brief overview focusing on General Fund portion
  of the Fiscal Year 2020-2021 Consolidated Budget.

  Keauonna Stovall-Buckhanon, Budget Manager, provided an overview of revenues and
  expenditures in the proposed annual budget for Fiscal Year 2020-2021.

  Following discussion, Mayor Butts ordered the report received and filed.

131.8  AGREEMENT NO. 20-267 APPROVED – 715 MALBOROUGH APARTMENTS,
  LLC. Staff report dated September 22, 2020, was presented recommending approval of
  an agreement with 715 Marlborough Apartments, LLC, to be recorded affecting real
  property with Affordable Housing Agreement (Density Bonus for incorporation of two
  (2) very-low income studio affordable units in development in exchange for certain
  development incentives) pursuant to the Density Bonus Ordinance and Density Bonus
  Law for that certain apartment building located at 715 Marlborough Avenue, Inglewood,
  CA 90302 restricting occupancy of units 11 and 12 to very-low income households at
  affordable rents.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 20-267; and 2) Authorize
  the Mayor to sign and execute Agreement No. 20-267 on behalf of the City. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
   Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  PUBLIC HEARING SET – AN APPEAL OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION
  DENIAL FOR SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2019-014 (SP-2019-014) TO ALLOW
  THE SALE OF BEER AND WINE FOR OFF-SITE CONSUMPTION FROM
  MARKET LOCATED AT 400 WEST MANCHESTER BOULEVARD. Staff report
  dated September 22, 2020, was presented requesting that a public hearing be set to
  consider an appeal of Planning Commission Denial for Special Use Permit No. 2019-014
  (SP-2019-014) to allow the sale of beer and wine for off-site consumption from an
  existing convenience market (Samy Mini Mart) located at 400 West Manchester
  Boulevard.

  Mayor Butts ordered the public hearing set for October 6, 2020, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

301  PUBLIC HEARING SET – AMENDMENTS TO INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL
  CODE CHAPTERS 8 AND 12 INCLUDING ZONING CODE AMENDMENT
  2018-01 TO ESTABLISH SHORT-TERM RENTAL REGULATIONS. Staff report
  dated September 22, 2020, was presented requesting that a public hearing be set to
  consider amendments to Inglewood Municipal Code Chapters 8 and 12 including Zoning
  Code Amendment 2018-01 (ZCA-2018-01) to establish Short-Term Rental regulations.

  Mayor Butts ordered the public hearing set for October 6, 2020, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

101  ORDINANCE NO. 20-16 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE FOR THE REASSIGNMENT OF CITY DUTIES. Staff report
  dated September 22, 2020, was presented recommending adoption of Ordinance No. 20-
  16 amending the Inglewood Municipal Code for the reassignment of City duties.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 20-16 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA AMENDING CHAPTER 2, ARTICLE 7 (CITY
  FUNDS – BUDGETARY PROCEDURES) AND ARTICLE 9 (CONDITIONS
  OF EMPLOYMENT); AMENDING CHAPTER 8, ARTICLE 3 (PERMITS);
  AND AMENDING CHAPTER 10, ARTICLE 5 (CURBS, SIDEWALKS AND
  PARKWAYS)

  which was introduced at the meeting held on September 15, 2020, be adopted. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132.6  CLOSED SESSION – LABOR NEGOTIATIONS WITH CONFIDENTIAL –
  ATTORNEY/CLIENT PRIVILEDGED; CONFERENCE WITH SERVICE
  EMPLOYEES INTERNATIONAL UNION (SEIU); INGLEWOOD POLICE
  OFFICERS ASSOCIATIONS (IPOA); INGLEWOOD POLICE MANAGEMENT
  ASSOCIATION (IPMA). Closed session – Confidential – Attorney/Client Privileged;
  Conference with Labor Negotiator Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6; Name
  of the Agency Negotiator: Jose O. Cortes, Human Resources Director; Name of
  Organizations Representing Employees; Service Employees International Union (SEIU);
  Inglewood Police Officers Associations (IPOA); Inglewood Police Management
  Association (IPMA).

  Status was given; Direction given to staff.
 127.1  EMERGENCY ORDER NO. 20-02 APPROVED – AUTHORIZING LICENSED
  CARD CLUBS TO OPERATE OUTDOORS; MAYOR TO EXECUTE ORDER
  ON BEHALF OF THE CITY AUTHORIZED. Emergency Order of the Inglewood
  City Council dated September 22, 2020, was presented authorizing Licensed Card Clubs
  to operate outdoors in accordance with State, County and City COVID-19 public health,
  safety and welfare regulations.

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Emergency Order No. 20-02; and 2)
  Authorize the Mayor to execute the Order on behalf of the City. The motion was carried
  by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.
  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Rick Ford commented that he would like the City Council to cancel rent. He also
  commented that he would like to see Community Room A re-opened.

  Caller (Name Unknown), spoke concerning the rent in the City of Inglewood.

  Gil Mathieu, District 4, spoke concerning the Clippers Arena.

  Carla (Last Name Unknown), suggested the City Council meetings should return to 7:00
  p.m.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in memory of US Airman Levi H. Thornhill, and Nyda Charlyn Fields, niece
  of City Manager Artie Fields, at the hour of 3:02 p.m.

  Approved this 4th day of May, 2021.

  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
